properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Austin/San Antonio has issued a
Flood Warning for the following rivers in Texas...

Pecos River Near Langtry affecting Val Verde County.

Devils River At Cauthorn Ranch Near Juno affecting Val Verde
County.

Pecos River At Pandale Crossing affecting Val Verde County.

Devils River At Bakers Crossing 19N Of Comstock affecting Val Verde
County.

Rio Grande At Foster Ranch affecting Val Verde County.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Devils River at Bakers Crossing 19N Of Comstock.

* WHEN...From Friday morning to late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...At 6.0 feet, (1.8 meters), Minor lowland flooding extends
into low areas of the flood plain with no significant impact. At
8.0 feet, (2.4 meters), Moderate lowland flooding reaches the
Highway 163 bridge floor several miles below Juno. This level is
turbulent and dangerous for inexperienced swimmers, canoeists and
kayakers. At 10.0 feet, (3.0 meters), Moderate lowland flooding is
several feet over the Bakers Crossing bridge at Highway 163. Flow
is well into the flood plain and very dangerous to campers and
river recreationists above Juno to Amistad Reservoir. At 12.0 feet,
(3.7 meters), Campers, automobiles and equipment near the river
above Juno to Amistad Reservoir can be washed downstream. The river
is very turbulent at this level and dangerous for inexperienced
swimmers, canoeists and kayakers. Five feet of flow covers the
Highway 163 bridge below Juno.


* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:15 AM CDT Thursday the stage was 2.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 4.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage
tomorrow morning to a crest of 11.5 feet tomorrow evening. It
will then fall below flood stage early Sunday afternoon.
- Flood stage is 6.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 900 PM CDT.

properties.headline: Freeze Watch issued October 15 at 7:54AM MDT until October 17 at 9:00AM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Frost Advisory, temperatures may briefly dip into
the lower to mid 30s resulting in frost formation or a light
freeze. For the Freeze Watch, a longer period of sub-freezing
temperatures in the mid 20s to around 30 degrees will be possible.

* WHERE...Eastern Fremont, Pueblo, Crowley, Otero, Las Animas,
Huerfano, Bent, Prowers and Baca Counties.

* WHEN...For the Frost Advisory, from 2 AM to 9 AM MDT Friday. For
the Freeze Watch, from late Friday night through Saturday morning.

* IMPACTS...Frost and freeze conditions could kill crops, other
sensitive vegetation and possibly damage unprotected outdoor
plumbing. Frost could harm sensitive outdoor vegetation. Sensitive
outdoor plants may be killed if left uncovered.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The coldest readings will occur Friday night
into Saturday morning with a killing freeze possible, which could
bring an end to the growing season.
properties.instruction:
Take steps now to protect tender plants from the cold.

To prevent water pipes from freezing; wrap or drain or allow them to
drip slowly.

properties.description:

* WHERE...Seminole County in east central Oklahoma...
Northwestern Hughes County in southeastern Oklahoma...

* WHEN...Until 1000 AM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 4 inches of rain have
fallen since last evening, and up to 9 inches of rain have fallen
since Wednesday morning.

the area. Minor flooding impacts will continue this morning.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Seminole, Wewoka, Konawa, Bowlegs, Cromwell, Little and Lima.

deaths occur in vehicles.

dangers of flooding.
